source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.12
text: Before sowing, seed can be disease-treated using a hot-water method to kill seed-borne pathogens: (1) Heat water using firewood/fire until it is hot, then let it come down from a full boil. (2) Check the water temperature with a thermometer and adjust until it reads about 60°C. (3) Submerge the sack of seed into the 60°C water and hold it there for about 10 minutes, stirring/turning the sack periodically so heating is even. (4) After exactly about 10 minutes, remove the seed sack from the hot water and immediately plunge it into cool/ambient-temperature water to stop the heat treatment. (5) Drain the seed and dry it in the shade. (6) The APPP project recommends this hot-water method as the standard way to sanitize seed and kill disease organisms before germinating and sowing it.
